title: Compact Recap UX — PRD Scrapbook
content:
Context and problem statement:

- Users in chat-style experiences frequently want a short, scannable recap at the end of a session: one-liner summary, 3 key bullets, and 1–2 suggested follow-ups. Current demos rely on manual prompts or brittle system messages.
- Goal: build a low-friction, opt-in "Compact Recap" feature that can be surfaced in the UI and via API. It should be cheap to compute, produce consistently useful recaps, and respect privacy/data retention rules.

User scenarios / jobs-to-be-done (informal):
- New user returns to a conversation after several days and wants the gist quickly.
- Customer support agent needs a concise summary to triage follow-ups.
- Product analytics wants a one-line anchor per conversation for downstream classification.

Core proposal (sketch):
1) UX: Add a lightweight "Recap" action in conversation header and an automatic end-of-session recap toggle (off by default). Recap option: One-line (headline), 3 bullets, 1 suggested next action. Secondary: toggle for "show sources" for context.
2) API: /v1/conversations/{id}/recap -> POST to request recap; response schema: {headline, bullets[], suggested_actions[]} (JSON). Support streaming for long recaps but default to compact.
3) Server-side modes:
   - Fast heuristic mode: small model or extractive approach (cheap) for immediate response.
   - Quality mode: generator model (larger) for better fluency and follow-ups (used when user selects 'improve recap').

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Extraction vs. Abstractive: extractive is cheaper and faithful but less natural. Abstractive improves readability but risks hallucinations. Could combine: extract key sentences then compress.
- When to auto-generate? Every session end vs on-demand. Auto increases compute but can be batched and cached.
- Privacy: if user opts out or workspace policy forbids summaries, must skip. Also ensure recaps don't persist beyond retention window unless explicitly saved.
- Multilingual: try to match user's language; otherwise fall back to English.

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Launch MVP where recaps are returned within 800ms p50 for heuristic mode for sessions under 3k tokens.
- Recap BLEU/ROUGE not great metric — prefer human evaluation: target 70% of sampled recaps rated "helpful" by annotators across 200 samples.
- Cost impact: <5% incremental token cost for active users in first 6 weeks (via batching + extractive fallback).

UX details / wireframe notes (text):
- Header control: small icon with tooltip "Recap: get a short summary of this conversation". Click opens inline card with headline (bold), bullets (inline), and CTA button "Save to Notes" / "Share".
- Inline hover: highlight sentences that were used to build the recap (if user toggles sources).
- Preferences: team-level default: off / on; user-level override.

Experiment plan (A/B):
- Cohort A: no recaps (control).
- Cohort B: on-demand recaps (button only).
- Cohort C: automatic recap at session end + on-demand.
Metrics to measure:
  - Primary: retention (7-day active rate), % users who click save/share, NPS change for power users.
  - Secondary: average session time, average tokens per session, support agent time-to-first-action (for CS pilot).

Implementation notes (engineering rough):
- Pipeline: conversation snapshot -> sentence boundary detection -> candidate sentence scoring (tf-idf / semantic embedding similarity) -> optional compression model -> format into headline + bullets.
- For heuristic mode: use embed-based clustering (small dimension) + pick centroids -> return original sentences as bullets.
- Cache key: conversation-id + conversation-hash + model-mode. Keep short TTL (24h) unless saved.
- Batch jobs: run end-of-day batch for sessions closed in last hour to precompute recaps for auto-mode users, limiting to sessions under 8k tokens.
- Fallback policy: if model call fails, return a best-effort extractive recap; if that fails, show "Recap unavailable" gracefully.

Privacy / compliance checklist (to confirm):
- Respect workspace data retention. Provide a flag allow_recaps_at_rest to opt into persistent recaps.
- Permission model: only visible to session participants and authorized agents.
- Audit logs: record recap generation events (who requested, model used, cost estimate).

Rollout / pilot idea:
- Stage 0: internal beta with marketing and support teams; gather qualitative feedback.
- Stage 1: small customer pilot (3 teams) using on-demand button + CS workflow.
- Stage 2: broader product release with auto-end-session toggle and API support.

Risks and mitigations:
- Hallucination risk: mitigate via conservative extractive-first default and "improve recap" button that triggers higher-quality generator.
- Cost runaway: mitigate with batching, extractive fallback, per-user rate limits, and size-based gating.
- UX confusion: run moderated usability tests; default to conservative wording ("Summary: may not include everything").

Follow-up tasks / TODOs:
- [ ] Prototype extractive pipeline with 1k sample conversations from internal dataset.
- [ ] Define annotation rubric and run 200-sample human eval.
- [ ] Wireframe UI and record micro-interactions.
- [ ] Draft API contract and OpenAPI spec for recap endpoint.
- [ ] Book 2-hour design review with Console/UX and Security.

Notes to self / ideas to explore later:
- Add a compact vector for each recap for downstream retrieval and classification.
- Try source highlighting via token-position mapping to enable "jump to original" in UI.
- Consider "timeline recaps" for very long multi-day sessions (day-by-day bullets).
- Experiment with offering multiple length options (headline-only, brief, long) with quick slider.

Snippets for pitch/email to pilot teams:
"We've built a lightweight, low-cost conversation recap that helps teams get to the gist faster. It's privacy-aware, can be toggled per-team, and integrates with existing notes. Would you pilot with support/product to measure time saved per ticket?"

End of notebook — this is messy, intentionally. Next step: turn top sections into a one-page PRD and add link to prototype results.
